title: The Warning Came in a Language Your Grandmother Doesn't Speak

body.en: A flood warning is broadcast on the radio, but only in English. Your grandmother, who lives with you, only understands Twi. What do you do?

choices.label: Translate the warning for her immediately and explain exactly what to do, in Twi
choices.consequence: Correct. An early warning that doesn't reach someone in a language they understand hasn't actually warned them at all — closing that gap yourself, right now, is what makes the warning system work for your household.

choices.label: Assume she'll understand the tone and urgency even without the words
choices.consequence: Not reliable. Tone alone doesn't tell her what to actually do — move to higher ground, gather documents, when to leave. She needs the actual instructions, translated.

choices.label: Wait for a Twi broadcast before telling her anything
choices.consequence: Too slow. Waiting for a translated broadcast that might not come in time wastes minutes she needs to prepare — translate it yourself now.
